_note: Config for components/answerer/run_answerer.py: the MuSiQue answering backend of issue #16. It scores a decomposition by whether executing it leads to the right final answer. The three methodology choices it encodes were made by Jahid on 2026-08-20 in session, pending supervisor confirmation, and are recorded in docs/adr/0019: (1) the reader is a model from the DECOMPOSER's registry (components/decomposer/models/<model>/config.json), default mistral_7b_instruct, swappable here or with --model; (2) the context for every sub-question is the MuSiQue item's full paragraph list, the standard answerable setting - there is no gold-supporting-only and no retrieval condition; (3) scoring is MuSiQue's official answer EM and answer F1 against the gold answer plus its alias list (src/answer_metrics.py). No model scores, rates or judges anything (CLAUDE.md standing constraint).
_reader_note: reader_models_dir_key names a repo.* key in configs/paths.json, so the reader reuses the decomposer's model registry: model_id, loader/quantization, decoding and post_process all come from that folder's config.json and no new model family is introduced (ADR 0019 decision 1). Only the prompt is the answerer's own, because a decomposition prompt cannot answer a question; it is one committed file for every model, split on chat_template.split_marker for a chat-template folder and joined for a plain one (see run_answerer.py::render_reader_template).
_context_note: policy 'all_paragraphs' is the only implemented policy and the only one that may ship (ADR 0019 decision 2): every paragraph of the MuSiQue item, in the item's own order, with no filtering by is_supporting and no retrieval. Any other value is refused rather than silently approximated. expected_paragraphs_per_item is a REPORTING reference, not an assertion: MuSiQue dev is 20 paragraphs per item for almost every item but not all of them (measured 2026-08-20 on musique_ans_v1.0_dev.jsonl: 2401 of 2417 rows have 20, and 16 rows have 17-19), so the run reports how many items carried fewer instead of refusing them.
_source_note: items_key is the MuSiQue file that carries the context paragraphs and the gold answer + aliases for an item (id, question, paragraphs, answer, answer_aliases). gold_decompositions_key is the gold-decomposition file used by --gold-decompositions, the oracle-decomposition ceiling: only the gold sub-question TEXT is read from it, never the gold sub-answers, so the ceiling measures the reader executing a perfect plan rather than a plan that already contains its answers.
_substitution_note: Each [#k] in a sub-question is replaced by the answer the reader produced for step k (src/step_lines.py::substitute_step_references). accept_bare_references also recognises MuSiQue's bare '#k', which is both the gold convention read by --gold-decompositions and, per ADR 0012 (target_reference_style 'as_is'), the style the fine-tuned arm emits; without it the oracle ceiling could not be executed at all. A reference with no answer yet (a forward reference, an out-of-range k, a failed or empty generation) is left in the text verbatim and counted, never dropped. dry_run_answer_template stands in for a generated answer under --dry-run so the substitution chain is exercised with no model loaded.
_answer_post_process_note: The reader is instructed to output the answer alone; this is the mechanical cleanup of what it actually returns, after the model folder's own post_process block (<think> stripping and truncate_at). max_answer_chars bounds a runaway answer before it is scored - a truncation, recorded per row and counted in the metrics, not a silent edit.
_generation_overrides_note: Applied on top of the model folder's generation block, identically for every sub-question. A MuSiQue answer is a short span, so the decomposer folders' decomposition-sized budget is not the right one here; a row that reached this budget is reported as rows_at_max_new_tokens.
_eval_set_note: The same pinned ADR 0007 evaluation set the decompositions were produced on: 200 items per hop depth for hops 2/3/4, 600 total, and exactly those ids. Asserted by identity, not only by count, with the shared assertion in run_decomposer.py (assert_pinned_eval_set) - an end-to-end number on a different set is not comparable to the decomposition-quality numbers or to another arm (ADR 0011). --gold-decompositions restricts itself to those ids for the same reason: the oracle ceiling has to be a ceiling for the set the arms ran on. --allow-unpinned-eval-set is the recorded opt-out for fixture and smoke runs, which are not experiment arms.
